## When are Each of the Estimands Different From Each Other

**When there is a correlation between number of schools per district and treatment effects, then the district weighted estimands are different from the school weighted estimands.**

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 6}
df.plot.estimands<-sruns.anal %>% filter(method=="DB_FE_Person", group=="sim_base_1") %>%
                                  mutate(ATE.district=ATE.super.district, 
                                         cor.strength.school=cor.strength.school*size.impact.cor.school) %>%
                                  dplyr::select(method,sim.id, all_of(vary_cols),
                                         ATE.super.school, ATE.super.student, 
                                         ATE.super.dist.school, ATE.super.dist.student) %>%
                                  pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("ATE.super"),
                                               names_to = "Estimand.type", values_to ="Estimand.values") %>%
                                separate(col=Estimand.type,into = c("junk","Estimand.type"),sep="ATE.") %>% 
                                dplyr::select(-junk)

ggplot(data=df.plot.estimands %>% filter(sim.id %in% c("size.impact.cor.district","base.values")))+
  geom_line(aes(y=Estimand.values,x=size.impact.cor.district,color=Estimand.type))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = .2, color="black", lty=2)+
  scale_y_continuous(limits =c(.12,.26),breaks = seq(.12,.26,.02))+
  labs(x="Correlation between Treatment Effect and District Size",
       y="Estimand Value")


```

## Mapping Estimators to Estimands

These simulations have the same base parameter values as the others but the correlation between school size and treatment effect is set at .75, with the idea that this should induce enough of a difference between the school and students weighted estimands.

## Which Estimators Produce the Same Values or Close to the Same Values
In all simulations that follow I've also increased the school and district treatment effect standard deviations to .3 in order to maxmize the differences between the school and student weighted estimands. 
Each row in the table are estimators that produce the same values 
```{r, include=T, eval=T, echo=F}

group_estimators <- function( rps,var ) {
  
  wid <-rps %>% dplyr::select( ID, method, all_of(var) ) %>% 
    pivot_wider( names_from = method, values_from = var ) %>%
    dplyr::select( -ID)
  
  results <- combn(names(wid), 2, function(x) {
    mean_diff <- mean(wid[[x[1]]] - wid[[x[2]]])
    tibble(pair = paste(x, collapse = " - "), mean_difference = round( mean_diff, digits=10 ) )
  }, simplify = FALSE) %>% bind_rows()
  
  
  # Create a matrix where each element is the mean difference between two columns
  mean_diff_matrix <- outer(1:ncol(wid), 1:ncol(wid), Vectorize(function(x, y) {
    abs( mean(wid[[x]] - wid[[y]]) )
  }))
  
  # Naming rows and columns for clarity
  colnames(mean_diff_matrix) <- names(wid)
  rownames(mean_diff_matrix) <- names(wid)
  
  mean_diff_matrix
  
  # Assuming mean_diff_matrix is your matrix of pairwise mean differences
  tolerance <- 10^-7
  
  # Create a binary matrix where 1 indicates differences below the tolerance
  binary_matrix <- 0 + (mean_diff_matrix < tolerance)
  binary_matrix
  
  # Convert this binary matrix into a list of groups
  groups <- list()
  already_included <- c()
  
  ests = sort( rownames(binary_matrix) )
  for (i in ests) {
    if (!( i %in% already_included)) {
      # Find indices where the estimator is within tolerance of others
      in_group <- which(binary_matrix[i, ] == 1)
      group_names <- colnames(binary_matrix)[in_group]
      groups[[length(groups) + 1]] <- group_names
      already_included <- c(already_included, group_names)
    }
  }
  groups
}

groups<-group_estimators(sruns.anal %>% filter(group=="estimators_estimand_2"), var= "mean.ATE.hat")

  relocate( grp ) %>%
  knitr::kable()

groups.se<-group_estimators(sruns.anal %>% filter(group=="estimators_estimand_2"), var= "mean.SE.hat")

map_chr( groups.se, paste, collapse = ", " ) %>%
```

This is the correlation across estimators once the ones that produce the same results are dropped
```{r, echo=FALSE,include=T,fig.width=8, fig.height= 6}
cor_mat <- function(d, value, lab=F) {
  d %>% 
    dplyr::select(ID, method, val={{value}}) %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from=method, values_from=val) %>% 
    dplyr::select(-ID) %>% 
    cor() %>% round(1) %>%
    ggcorrplot::ggcorrplot(type="lower", 
                           lab = lab,
                           show.diag=T) 
}


#print("Correlations Across ATE Estimates ")
cor_mat(sruns %>% filter(group=="estimators_estimand_2", method %in% core.selected), mean.ATE.hat, lab=T)
```

## Confirming School versus Student targeted estimators

The same as in the analysis above, consistently:

**The school targeted estimators are: DB_FE_Cluster, MLM_FE, MLM_FI_Block, MLM_FI_Cluster, MLM_FI_Person, MLM_FIRC, MLM_RE, MLM_RIRC **

**The student targeted estimators are: DB_FE_Person, DB_FI_Person_Block, DB_FI_Person_Person, DB_HT, DB_Raj,LR_FI_CRVE_Cluster, LR_FI_CRVE_Person**

*The MLM estimators aren't really student targeted when the ICC is low, they're really closest to the school weighted estimand the whole time. However, they do seem to be weighting between the student and school estimands and as the school ICC goes up they become more school weighted.

## How biased are the student weighted estimators as the correlation between school size and treatment effect increases

Here are simulation with the non-varying parameter values back at the base values. Even large correlations between the ATE and the school size do not lead to substantially biased estimates from the student targeted estimators. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 6}
stu.selected = c("DB_FE_Person", "DB_FI_Person_Block", "DB_FI_Person_Person", 
                             "DB_HT", "DB_Raj","LR_FI_CRVE_Cluster", "LR_FI_CRVE_Person")

sruns.plot.stu<-sruns.anal %>% filter(group=="sim_base_1" & method %in% stu.selected) %>%
                          mutate(ATE.district=ATE.super.district,
                                 cor.strength.school=cor.strength.school*size.impact.cor.school) %>% 
  dplyr::select(method,sim.id, all_of(vary_cols),bias.f.stu) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("bias"),names_to = "bias.type", values_to ="bias")%>%
  separate(col=bias.type,into = c("junk","bias.type"),sep="bias.f.")%>% dplyr::select(-junk)

ggplot(data=sruns.anal %>% 
         filter(sim.id %in% c("cor.strength.school","base.values") & group=="sim_base_1" & method %in% stu.selected))+
  geom_smooth(aes(color=method,y=bias.f.stu,x=cor.strength.school ),se=F)+
  geom_hline(yintercept =0,lty=2,color="black")+
    scale_y_continuous(limits =c(-.018,.015),breaks = round(seq(-.015,.01,.005),3))+
  labs(x="Correlation between School Size and ATE", y="Bias in Student Weighted Estimand")
  
```  
## Simulation Parameters

The simulation currently takes in the following parameters. The base value is the value across simulations where the value doesn't vary.

K: The total number of districts \newline
K base value: `r base.values$K`

J.bar: The average number of schools per district. This must be at least 6.\newline
J.bar base value: `r base.values$J.bar`

p.bar: The average proportion of schools treated in a district \newline
p.bar base value: `r base.values$p.bar`

ATE.district: The average treatment effect \newline
ATE.district base value: `r base.values$ATE.district`

sd.district: The district standard deviation in the treatment effect \newline
sd.district base value: `r base.values$sd.district`

ICC.district: The district level ICC \newline
ICC.district base value: `r base.values$ICC.district`

variable.J: Indicator for whether the number of schools per district varies \newline
variable.J base value: `r base.values$variable.J`

variable.p: Indicator for whether the proportion of schools treated per district varies\newline
variable.p base value: `r base.values$variable.p`

n.bar: The average number of students per school. \newline 
n.bar base value: `r base.values$n.bar`

ICC.school: The school level ICC \newline
ICC.school base value: `r base.values$ICC.school`

variable.n: Indicator for whether the number of students per school varies\newline
variable.n base value: `r base.values$variable.n`

size.impact.cor.district: Correlation between the number of schools in a district and treatment effect \newline
size.impact.cor.district base value: `r base.values$size.impact.cor.district`

proptx.impact.cor.district: Correlation between the proportion of schools treated in a district and treatment effect \newline
proptx.impact.cor.district base value: `r base.values$proptx.impact.cor.district`

size.intercept.cor.district:Correlation between the number of schools in a district and district average outcome value \newline
size.intercept.cor.district base value: `r base.values$size.intercept.cor.district`

size.impact.cor.school: Correlation between the number of students per schools and treatment effect \newline
size.impact.cor.school base value: `r base.values$size.impact.cor.school`
